chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of it from Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd, from his father, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ghālib, from Saʿd al-Iskāf, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

“Whichever believer washes a believer and says, when turning him: ‘O Allah, this is the body of Your believing servant. You have taken his soul out from him and separated the two of them, so Your pardon, Your pardon’—Allah will forgive him the sins of a year, except the major sins.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: When he has finished the three washings, he casts over him a clean cloth and dries him. Its mention has already passed. Then he said: Then he withdraws to one side and washes his hands up to his elbows, and turns to the shrouds that he had prepared for him, spreading them upon something pure. He places the outer garment or the wrapping cloth that serves in its place—and it is the outermost one—and spreads it out, sprinkling upon it some of the powdered perfume he had prepared. Then he places the other wrapping cloth over it and sprinkles upon it some of the powdered perfume, and places the shirt upon the waist-wrapper and sprinkles upon it some of the powdered perfume, using much of it. Then he returns to the deceased and transfers him from the place in which he washed him until he places him in his shirt. He takes some cotton, places upon it some of the powdered perfume, and puts it on the outlet of excrement. He places some cotton with powdered perfume upon his private part, and fastens it with the cloth that we mentioned, fastening it firmly to his hips so that nothing may come out from him. He takes the cloth that we called a waist-wrapper and wraps it upon him from his navel to wherever it reaches of his shins, just as a living person wraps himself, so that it is above the cloth with which he fastened the cotton. He then goes to the camphor that he prepared for his embalmment and crushes it with his hand, placing some of it on his forehead upon which he used to prostrate to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He places some of it on the tip of his nose by which he used to press himself down for Him in prostration. He places some of it on the inner sides of his palms, wiping with it his palms and their fingers with which he used to meet the earth in his prostration. He places it on the two knees and on the outer side of the toes of his feet, because they are among his places of prostration. If any camphor remains, he uncovers his shirt from his chest, casts it upon it, and wipes him with it, then returns the shirt after that to its state. He takes the two fresh palm-sticks, puts some cotton upon them, and places one of them on his right side alongside his collarbone, attaching it to his skin, and places the other on his left side between the shirt and the waist-wrapper.

key_terms.الذَّرِيرَةِ: a powdered perfume sprinkled on the shroud and cotton
key_terms.الْأَكْفَانِ: the shrouds used to wrap the deceased
key_terms.الْجَرِيدَتَيْنِ: the two fresh palm-sticks placed with the deceased
key_terms.الْغَسَلَاتِ الثَّلَاثِ: the three washings performed for the deceased
key_terms.الْكَافُورِ: camphor used in the embalming and ritual preparation of the deceased
key_terms.تَحْنِيطِهِ: the embalming or perfuming of the deceased with camphor
key_terms.عَفْوَكَ: Your pardon; a plea for divine forgiveness
key_terms.غَسَّلَ: performed the ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What should be said and done when washing and shrouding a deceased believer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith describes both the spiritual merit and the practical procedure of washing and shrouding a deceased believer. It includes a du'a for the one performing the ghusl of the dead and then details the steps of drying, perfuming, shrouding, applying camphor, and placing the two palm-sticks.
